draft.title: Causes of mutation
card: A mutation is a change in the base sequence of DNA. Some mutations happen with no outside cause, and others are triggered by something in the environment.
a mutation that happens by chance, most often as a mistake when DNA is copied before a cell divides. The copying enzymes are accurate but not perfect.
anything that raises the rate of mutation. Examples are ultraviolet light from the sun, ionising radiation such as X-rays, and some chemicals, including those in tobacco smoke.
A mutagen does not guarantee a mutation in a given cell. It makes mutations more likely, and cells can often repair the damage before it becomes permanent.
draft.remember: Mutations arise from copying errors or from mutagens, which raise the chance of a change.

a.q: Which statement best describes a mutagen?
opts: It increases the rate at which mutations occur
It is a mutation that has been inherited
It is an error that only happens when DNA is copied
It is a change that always damages a gene
a.why: A mutagen is any agent that makes mutations more likely, such as ultraviolet light. Copying errors are a different, spontaneous cause, so saying mutagens are only copying errors is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what a mutagen does to the chance of a mutation.

b.q: Priya spends years working outdoors without sun protection, and a skin cell develops a mutation. Which explanation fits best?
opts: Ultraviolet light raised the chance of a DNA change
Ultraviolet light forced a mutation in every skin cell
The mutation must have been a copying error, not a mutagen
Mutations only occur in cells that are not dividing
b.why: Ultraviolet light is a mutagen, so it raises the likelihood of DNA changes in exposed cells. It does not force a mutation in every cell, because it only increases the chance and cells can repair some damage.
b.clue: A mutagen changes the chance, not the certainty.

a.best: It increases the rate at which mutations occur

b.best: Ultraviolet light raised the chance of a DNA change

problems.detail: Both wrong options turn on absolute words ('always damages', 'only happens'), while the card says a mutagen makes mutations more likely. Students can rule them out by spotting the absolute word rather than by knowing what a mutagen is.
All three wrong options use absolute words ('only occur', 'forced... every', 'must have been'). The one hedged option stands out, so the answer can be found without the idea.
The clue 'A mutagen changes the chance, not the certainty' nearly states the correct option, which is the only one that talks about chance.
The why says UV 'only increases the chance'. This adds an absolute word where the card says a mutagen 'makes mutations more likely'. The meaning is accurate, but the wording could be softened.

The remember line sorts causes neatly into 'copying errors or mutagens'. The card says spontaneous mutations are only 'most often' copying errors, so the line splits the ideas more cleanly than the card does.

check.summary: The facts are correct and each question has one clear right answer. However, both questions let students eliminate wrong options by their absolute words ('always', 'only', 'forced', 'must'), and question b's clue nearly gives the answer away. The remember line also simplifies spontaneous mutations to copying errors alone.

anything that raises the rate of mutation. Examples are ultraviolet light from the sun, ionising radiation such as X-rays, and some chemicals, including those in tobacco smoke.

proposal.remember: Some mutations arise by chance. Mutagens make mutations more likely but do not guarantee one.

opts: An agent that raises the rate of mutation
A copying mistake made as DNA is replicated
An enzyme that repairs damage to DNA
A change in the base sequence of DNA
a.why: A mutagen, such as ultraviolet light, is an agent that makes mutations more likely. A copying mistake is a spontaneous mutation, which happens by chance with no outside cause, so it is not a mutagen.
a.clue: Is a mutagen the change itself, or something acting on DNA?

b.q: Two skin cells on Priya's arm get the same exposure to sunlight. One develops a mutation and the other does not. Which explanation fits best?
opts: UV makes mutations more likely, and some damage is repaired
UV acts as a mutagen in some skin cells but not others
The second cell was shaded from the sun's UV light
UV light lowered the mutation rate in the second cell
b.why: Ultraviolet light is a mutagen, so it raises the chance of a mutation in every exposed cell without guaranteeing one, and cells can often repair damage. Saying UV is a mutagen in some cells but not others is tempting, but a mutagen raises the rate in all exposed cells. The outcome in each cell comes down to chance and repair.
b.clue: Think about what cells can do after their DNA is damaged.

a.best: An agent that raises the rate of mutation

b.best: UV makes mutations more likely, and some damage is repaired
